# Phase 20 R2 item 4 -- one SMP1345-079LF in a gapped patch, ON vs OFF (NOT a design)

**Labels: MODEL_ONLY, NOT_HFSS_VALIDATED, PROVISIONAL_DATASHEET** (datasheet covers 10 MHz-6 GHz; 8-12 GHz is an extrapolation). Generated by `scripts/research/phase20_r2_demo.py`. Cell: R1 demo cell (10 mm, RT5880 1.575 mm tan d 0.0009, PEC ground), 8 x 8 mm patch cut by a 1 mm gap, bridged only by a 0.5 mm wide strip carrying the diode (ideal series model, span 1 mm, `transverse_conducts=False`); mesh 40 x 40, Floquet 24; S at the pattern plane z = 0; phi = 0 (TM: E along x, across the gap).

## Loss (1 - reflected power; includes the 0.0009 substrate loss that a lossless cell would not show)
* theta 0 TM: ON max 0.012, OFF max 0.011; min |S11| ON 0.994, OFF 0.995
* theta 0 TE: ON max 0.011, OFF max 0.011; min |S11| ON 0.995, OFF 0.995
* theta 30 TM: ON max 0.011, OFF max 0.014; min |S11| ON 0.995, OFF 0.993
* theta 30 TE: ON max 0.013, OFF max 0.013; min |S11| ON 0.994, OFF 0.994
* theta 60 TM: ON max 0.010, OFF max 0.021; min |S11| ON 0.995, OFF 0.989
* theta 60 TE: ON max 0.027, OFF max 0.023; min |S11| ON 0.987, OFF 0.988

**TE vs the R1 8 mm strip:** TE ON-OFF phase difference is at most 0.6 deg below 12 GHz and TE absorption is at most 0.027 (substrate loss included), against up to 0.68 absorbed with the R1 full-width load at 60 deg. A diode-sized (0.5 mm) bridge removes the circulating-current path: TE is nearly independent of the diode state. At 12 GHz and 60 deg the TE ON-OFF phase is 8.7 deg (see the discretisation note).

## Sensitivity at 10 GHz: +-20 % one parameter at a time (change of the co-pol S11 phase vs the nominal state, deg; TM, theta 0 / 30 / 60)
* off:C_T x0.8: +116.8 / +143.6 / -164.4
* off:C_T x1.2: -27.0 / -28.3 / -35.0
* off:L_s x0.8: +34.1 / +40.6 / +66.0
* off:L_s x1.2: -19.4 / -20.7 / -26.5
* off:Rp 10k (assumed): -0.1 / -0.1 / -0.2
* off:Rp 3k (assumed): -0.7 / -0.9 / -1.6
* on:1mA (Rs 3.5): -0.0 / -0.0 / -0.0
* on:L_s x0.8: +1.5 / +1.3 / +1.1
* on:L_s x1.2: -1.3 / -1.1 / -0.9
* on:R_s x0.8: +0.0 / +0.0 / +0.0
* on:R_s x1.2: -0.0 / -0.0 / -0.0

R_p entries are `ASSUMED_SENSITIVITY_NOT_DEVICE_DATA`; `on:1mA` is the datasheet's 1 mA R_s. **OFF is NOT robust:** it sits near the L_s-C_T series resonance (13.8 GHz nominal), so +-20 % on C_T or L_s moves the phase by tens of degrees up to over 100 deg (the 0.8 x C_T case crosses the +-180 deg wrap); C_T at 0 V is not given and may be higher than the 0.19 pF used. ON is robust (R_s irrelevant, L_s +-1.5 deg).

## Discretisation (mesh 40 vs 80; the only two meshes whose cell edges hit the 0.5 mm strip edges)
* ON TM: max |phase(80) - phase(40)| = 0.38 deg (at 12 GHz, theta 0); max |d abs| 0.0002
* ON TE: max |phase(80) - phase(40)| = 7.39 deg (at 10 GHz, theta 60); max |d abs| 0.0060
* OFF TM: max |phase(80) - phase(40)| = 2.02 deg (at 10 GHz, theta 60); max |d abs| 0.0002
* OFF TE: max |phase(80) - phase(40)| = 7.54 deg (at 10 GHz, theta 60); max |d abs| 0.0011

R1's practice (Richardson with the observed order from three meshes) could not be repeated: meshes 60 and 100 put the strip edges mid-cell (the solver warns) and gave non-monotone results (the OFF TM phase read -157 / -180 / -156 deg on 40 / 60 / 80), so they were dropped; with two meshes no order is observable and **no extrapolation is made**. The stated uncertainty of the tables above is therefore the 40 -> 80 difference. TE phase at 60 deg is the worst (several degrees); the ON-OFF TE statement above is robust to it because ON and OFF share the same TE error.
